harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1 (RHEL 7.9), installed lvm2 (via a temporary CentOS 7 vault repo since subscription-manager repos were disabled), built an LVM stack backed by two file-backed loop devices (no spare disk/partition existed — root partition was fully allocated), created VG vg_data and LV lv_data, formatted XFS, mounted at /srv/data, wrote test data, then grew the LV online from 900M to ~2.15GiB (filesystem to 2.2G) using vgextend+lvextend+xfs_growfs while the volume stayed mounted, with data integrity verified via sha256 checksums before and after. A systemd oneshot unit (lvm-loop-setup.service) was added to reattach the loop devices and activate the VG at boot, since loop devices don't persist automatically. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id/uptime/mount/checksum evidence, issued `shutdown -r now` in the background so the ack returned before disconnection, polled until SSH access returned, confirmed the boot_id and boot time changed (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and verified post-restart that the LV, VG, mount, and both test files (checksums) were all fully intact and healthy.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 disk layout and OS (RHEL 7.9, root partition using all 20G disk, lvm2 not installed)
Added a temporary CentOS 7 vault yum repo and installed lvm2 and dependencies
Created two file-backed loop devices (disk0.img=1000M, disk1.img=1500M) as LVM PVs since no spare disk/partition existed
pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate'd a 900M lv_data in vg_data, formatted XFS, mounted at /srv/data, added fstab entry
Wrote a text file, a 200MB random bigfile, and a sha256 checksum manifest as test data
Extended vg_data with the second loop PV, lvextend'd lv_data to ~2.15GiB, and xfs_growfs'd the filesystem online while mounted
Verified post-grow data integrity via sha256sum -c (both files OK) and confirmed mount stayed active throughout
Created and enabled a systemd oneshot unit (lvm-loop-setup.service) to reattach loop devices and vgchange -ay at boot for persistence across restarts
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, mount state, df, lvs, checksums, loop device mapping, fstab, service enablement
Issued a backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' on node1 so the exec ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until command execution was available again, confirming SSH downtime then recovery
Verified boot_id and uptime -s changed (new boot identity), proving an actual OS restart occurred

Re-verified post-restart: mount active, df shows 2.2G filesystem, lvs/vgs show LV intact across both loop PVs, loop devices auto-reattached, checksums both OK, and lvm-loop-setup.service ran successfully at boot

evidence.summary: mount/df output shows /dev/vg_data/lv_data mounted at /srv/data with 897M size immediately after creation

evidence.requirement: Grow LV to >=2GB while mounted, contents intact
evidence.summary: vgextend+lvextend+xfs_growfs executed live on the mounted filesystem, growing LV to <2.15GiB (2.2G filesystem); subsequent sha256sum -c on bigfile and testfile.txt both report OK and mount remained active, confirming contents stayed intact during online growth

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity + service/data health)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 2fc81aed-3ce8-4a35-8f4c-b73206afa45f, uptime -s 23:26:29, mount/df/lvs showing healthy 2.2G mounted LV, checksums OK, and loop device mapping before reboot
Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned ack:0 immediately, and the following exec call confirmed the node was mid-reboot (SSH connection timed out)

evidence.requirement: Node down during reboot / boot identity changed
evidence.summary: Two consecutive polls show SSH connection timed out (node offline), then a poll succeeds with new boot_id c55201d2-7fb6-4ae4-a0d2-0fd643e33975 and new uptime -s 23:33:00, proving an actual restart occurred (not just a service bounce)

After restart: mount shows /srv/data active with 2.2G XFS filesystem, lvs/vgs show lv_data intact spanning both loop PVs, losetup -a shows both loop devices auto-reattached, sha256sum -c reports both test files OK, and lvm-loop-setup.service shows active (exited)/SUCCESS confirming the boot-time reattachment/activation worked
